title: Training a Support Vector Machine for Bacterial Cell Detection in Microscopy Images
author: Steemans, Govers

steps.title: Install Anaconda
steps.instruction: Download the appropriate Anaconda installer for Windows from https://www.anaconda.com/products/individual and follow the OS‑specific installation instructions.

steps.title: Create Python virtual environment
steps.instruction: Open an Anaconda Prompt, then create a new environment named svm_env with Python 3.10.8 by running: conda create --name svm_env python=3.10.8 and answer “y” when prompted to proceed.

steps.title: Activate env and install libraries
steps.instruction: Activate the newly created environment and install the exact library versions required for the notebooks.

substeps.instruction: conda activate svm_env
pip install numpy==1.23.4
pip install pandas==2.0.1
pip install tifffile==2022.10.10
pip install tqdm==4.64.1
pip install opencv-python-headless==4.6.0.66
pip install scikit-image==0.19.3
pip install scipy==1.9.3
pip install shapely==2.0.1
pip install scikit-learn==1.1.3
pip install matplotlib==3.6.2

steps.title: Install and launch Jupyter Notebook
steps.instruction: Within the same environment install Jupyter, answer “y” to the prompt, then start the notebook server.

substeps.instruction: conda install jupyter   (answer y when asked “Proceed ([y]/n)?”)
jupyter notebook

steps.title: Install Git and clone repository
steps.instruction: Download Git for Windows from https://git-scm.com/downloads, open a regular Command Prompt (not Anaconda Prompt), and clone the protocol repository.

substeps.instruction: git clone https://github.com/Govers-Lab/Steemans_and_Govers_2023.git

steps.title: Run feature extraction notebook
steps.instruction: Execute the feature extraction pipeline to generate a DataFrame of 26 cellular features and save it as a pickle file.

substeps.instruction: Activate the svm_env environment (conda activate svm_env).
Launch Jupyter Notebook (jupyter notebook).
In the file browser open Notebooks/feature_extraction.ipynb inside the cloned Steemans_and_Govers_2023 folder.
Run every cell in order:
a) Import the required Python libraries (first cell).
b) Load raw phase‑contrast images (TIF files) by providing the folder path; load cell‑mesh data by providing its path and filename.
c) Load the helper functions that compute the features (included in the notebook).
d) Execute the feature‑extraction cell to compute the 26 features for each cell mesh.
e) Save the resulting DataFrame to a pickle file; set the file_path so the filename ends with “svm_features.pkl”.

steps.title: Compute cell geometric features
steps.instruction: Calculate shape‑related descriptors from the extracted mesh data.

substeps.instruction: Total cell length (µm): compute the distance between midpoints of each mesh segment (x1,y1)-(x2,y2) and sum all step lengths.
Cell width (µm): take the mean of the top one‑third of segment widths (distances between (x1,y1) and (x2,y2)).
Cell area (µm²): calculate the polygon area of the cell contour using shapely.Polygon().
Cell volume (µm³): treat each segment as a cylinder, compute its volume with the trapezoidal rule, and sum over all segments.
Cell surface area (µm²): for each cylindrical segment compute 2·π·(width/2)²·step_length and sum the results.
Max, min and mean contour curvature (µm⁻¹): obtain curvature from the first and second derivatives of the contour coordinates.
Cell perimeter (µm): sum Euclidean distances between consecutive subpixel contour points.
Cell circularity: calculate 4·π·area / perimeter².
Cell compactness: calculate perimeter² / area.
Cell sphericity: calculate 1.5·π·perimeter² / (π·1.5·area) (as given in the original text).

steps.title: Compute phase‑contrast intensity features
steps.instruction: Derive intensity‑based descriptors from the phase‑contrast images using the cell contours.

substeps.instruction: Total phaco intensity (A.U.): sum all inverted phase‑contrast pixel values inside the cell contour after subtracting the mean intensity of the background (outside all cell masks).
Max and mean phaco intensity (A.U.): compute the maximum and average pixel values inside the contour.
Phaco contour intensity peaks (count): apply scipy.signal.find_peaks() to the intensity profile along the contour and count the peaks.
Max, min and mean contour intensity (A.U.): obtain the extreme and average values of the intensity profile along the contour.
Contour intensity variability (A.U.): compute a rolling‑window standard deviation with window size 10 over the contour intensity values; report the maximum and mean of these standard deviations.
Midline intensity skewness: calculate the skewness of the intensity distribution along the cell midline.
Midline intensity kurtosis: calculate the kurtosis of the intensity distribution along the cell midline.
Max and mean expanded contour intensity (A.U.): expand the cell contour outward by 2 pixels, then compute the maximum and average intensity along this expanded contour.

Mean cell edge gradient (A.U.): generate both an expanded and an eroded contour, subtract the intensity values of the eroded contour from those of the expanded contour at each point, and average the differences.
